headline: Nvidia is reportedly in talks either to put more money into the AI start-up Reflection AI or to buy it outright.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: the headline matches the facts (early talks, reported by the FT), a possible takeover by the main AI chip maker of a leading US open-model developer.
importance_line: What changed is that Nvidia is reportedly weighing full ownership of a leading US developer of open AI models, which matters first to developers and governments that rely on open models, then to rival chip and model makers, and the doubt is that the talks are early, rest on unnamed sources and neither company has commented.
summary: The Financial Times reported on 10 Oct 2026, citing people with direct knowledge, that Nvidia is in early talks to deepen its investment in Reflection AI or buy the start-up, which it has already backed with $800 million; Reuters, relaying the report, said it could not immediately verify it. Reflection, founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers, makes open-weight AI models (models whose trained parameters are published so others can run them), and the FT says one route is an "acqui-hire", hiring its staff and licensing its technology rather than buying it outright, which could avoid a lengthy regulatory review, with an agreement possible within weeks or the talks still falling apart.
notes: Reuters page blocked (HTTP 401); the Reuters text was read on The Economic Times, with Startup Fortune as cross-check. The first reporter is the Financial Times (paywalled, not read), so the credit is FT as relayed by Reuters. Startup Fortune also names Bloomberg as reporting the talks.
